description: 110 first-person traits. First 60 = initial blind questionnaire (balanced across 11 domains). Remaining 50 = refining questions available after the first 60. Mate-preference step follows. Preference matching only.

traits.definition: I usually stay composed and steady when things become stressful or uncertain.
My mood tends to stay even; I do not swing rapidly between emotional highs and lows.
I feel emotions strongly and quickly; small events can produce large emotional responses.
I am easily bothered or distressed by criticism, setbacks, or tense situations.
I tend to become irritated or angry more quickly than most people.
I generally expect things to work out well and look for the positive side of situations.
When I say I will do something, I almost always follow through.
I like to plan ahead and keep my responsibilities and surroundings in order.
I prefer to keep plans flexible and decide things in the moment rather than sticking to fixed schedules.
I notice and care about small details that many people overlook.
I can stick to routines and long-term goals even when motivation dips.
I have strong goals and push myself to achieve and improve over time.
I naturally express warmth and affection toward people I care about.
I easily sense and feel what others are feeling and am moved by their experiences.
People close to me generally find me a reliable source of emotional support.
I keep my feelings more private and do not readily show affection or strong emotion.
I feel a strong desire to help when I see someone suffering or in need.
I tend to give people the benefit of the doubt and expect good intentions.
I am comfortable stating my needs and opinions clearly, even when others disagree.
I often adjust my own preferences to keep harmony or meet others' needs.
I am good at setting and maintaining personal boundaries with others.
In joint decisions I tend to take the lead and push for my preferred direction.
I am often content to let someone else take the lead on plans and decisions.
I can say no to requests without feeling excessive guilt or needing long explanations.
I prefer to address issues head-on and say what I mean without much softening.
I carefully choose words to avoid unnecessary conflict or hurt feelings.
I go out of my way to avoid arguments or tense confrontations.
I can wait and stay calm when progress is slow or others are difficult.
I am able to let go of past hurts and move forward without holding lasting grudges.
I tend to bring up small irritations before they grow into bigger problems.
I value honesty highly and prefer to speak the truth even when it is uncomfortable.
I have strong personal principles and try to live by them consistently.
I try to treat people impartially and consider different sides before judging.
Once I commit to a person or cause, I stay steadfast through difficulties.
When I make a commitment I treat it as binding even if circumstances become inconvenient.
I prefer to handle most things myself and do not easily ask for help.
I like building a shared life where we rely on and support each other daily.
I need a clear sense of personal space and autonomy even inside a close relationship.
My close relationships are a central source of meaning and priority in my life.
I genuinely enjoy and look forward to stretches of time spent completely alone.
Being around other people usually leaves me feeling more energetic and alive.
I need regular time alone to feel restored; too much social contact drains me.
I feel at ease and can be myself in group settings and social gatherings.
I much prefer deep conversation with one or two people over large group interaction.
After social time I need solitude to feel restored before I want more interaction.
I am driven to explore new ideas, places, or experiences and get bored with too much routine.
I am most comfortable with familiar routines, known environments, and proven ways of doing things.
I enjoy thinking about complex ideas and learning for its own sake.
I adapt relatively easily when plans, environments, or expectations shift.
I actively seek out new knowledge or skills even when there is no immediate practical need.
I enjoy teasing, joking, and bringing a light or playful spirit into interactions.
I often notice and share the funny side of situations.
I tend to approach life and conversations in a serious, earnest way.
I find humor in everyday situations and laugh more readily than many people.
I use light teasing as a way of showing fondness and creating connection.
I feel a strong need to understand the deeper purpose or significance of my life and choices.
I prefer to live in the moment and do not spend much time questioning the larger meaning of existence.
Awareness of life’s limits and impermanence often influences how I make decisions or set priorities.
I feel drawn to spiritual, philosophical, or transcendent questions beyond everyday practical concerns.
I focus mainly on practical, this-world matters and am not strongly drawn to spiritual or ultimate questions.
I tend to focus on practical risks and prefer not to assume the best outcome.
After a setback or upset I tend to bounce back fairly quickly.
I often replay past events or worries in my mind long after they have happened.
I can usually name what I am feeling and why while the feeling is still present.
I am satisfied with a moderate level of achievement and do not feel driven to constantly climb higher.
I work best when there is a clear deadline and can lose focus without one.
I often put off starting or finishing tasks even when I know they matter.
I like creating systems, lists, or habits that make daily life run more smoothly.
I am cautious about trusting others until they have clearly earned it.
I naturally express care through touch, closeness, or physical warmth.
When someone is talking I focus fully and try to understand before responding.
I often keep an emotional distance even with people I care about.
I am willing to stay in a difficult conversation until the issue is clearer.
In group or pair decisions I often let others take the lead rather than push my view.
I guard my time and energy and am selective about what I commit to.
When I set a limit I often feel the need to justify it at length.
When tension rises I am more likely to pull away than to engage.
I find it relatively easy to apologize when I have hurt or inconvenienced someone.
I notice and remember imbalances in effort or fairness over time.
In disagreements I push for clear understanding of what each person actually means.
I prefer to be open about my motives and feelings rather than strategic or hidden.
I judge right and wrong partly by the specific situation rather than fixed rules alone.
Loyalty from and to the people close to me is one of my highest priorities.
I speak up when I see something I consider unfair, even if it creates friction.
I hold strong values but rarely discuss or display them unless asked.
In a close relationship I naturally want frequent contact and updates.
I prefer major life decisions to be made together rather than by one person alone.
I can regulate my own mood and do not rely heavily on a partner to feel okay.
I tend to blend my routines, plans, and preferences with a partner’s quite readily.
Even in a close relationship I keep distinct hobbies, friendships, or projects of my own.
In conversation I tend to speak more than I listen and enjoy keeping the talk going.
I am social with a small circle and prefer not to expand it much.
I like bringing people together and creating shared social experiences.
In groups I am content to be present without needing to perform or stand out.
I am usually the one who suggests getting together or making social plans.
I trust methods and ideas that have already been proven more than experimental ones.
I notice and care about beauty, atmosphere, or sensory quality in my surroundings.
I enjoy discussing abstract ideas, possibilities, and ‘what if’ scenarios.
I prefer concrete, useful thinking over abstract or theoretical discussion.
I can hear constructive criticism without becoming defensive most of the time.
I am more comfortable with serious or sincere conversation than with banter or silliness.
I am happy to drop plans or change direction if a more fun opportunity appears.
My sense of humor tends to be understated, ironic, or dry rather than loud or physical.
In tense or heavy moments I often try to lighten the mood.
I often take statements at face value and can miss playful or sarcastic intent.
I learn and decide best by doing and experiencing things directly rather than by thinking them through first.
I actively try to notice and enjoy ordinary moments as they happen instead of rushing past them.
I feel most alive when I am trying something new, uncertain, or physically engaging.
I trust my body and senses as important guides for how to live, not only my thoughts or plans.
I prefer to keep life open and respond to what arises rather than mapping out a detailed long-term life plan.
I am primarily looking for a committed long-term relationship.
Marriage is an important possible endpoint for my relationship.
I am comfortable keeping dating casual without aiming quickly toward commitment.
I want an exclusive romantic relationship.
I am genuinely open to consensual non-monogamy.
I prefer relationships to develop slowly before major commitments.
I prefer relationships to become serious relatively quickly.
I want to have children in the future.
I do not want to have children.
I would seriously consider adoption as a way of becoming a parent.
I am comfortable becoming a parent to a partner's existing children.
I would ideally like to have a relatively large family.
Becoming a parent is important enough to strongly influence my choice of partner.
I want extended family to play a significant role in our shared life.
Sexual compatibility is a major part of a satisfying relationship for me.
I want frequent physical affection in a relationship.
Romantic gestures and deliberate romance matter substantially to me.
I generally want sex relatively frequently in a relationship.
I am comfortable discussing sexual preferences and boundaries openly.
I expect sexual exclusivity in a committed relationship.
Strong sexual chemistry is necessary for me to pursue a serious relationship.
I naturally prefer an early daily schedule.
I naturally prefer a late daily schedule.
I am happiest spending much of my free time at home.
I want an active social life with frequent outings and events.
Travel and experiencing different places are important parts of the life I want.
I strongly prefer building a stable life in one place.
I prefer living in a city with substantial services and activity nearby.
I prefer a rural or low-density environment.
I prefer leaving room for spontaneous changes rather than planning everything.
I prefer a predictable, planned daily life.
Physical activity and an active lifestyle are important to me.
Financial security is a major priority in how I structure my life.
I naturally prioritize saving money over discretionary spending.
I am comfortable spending money on experiences, interests, or enjoyment.
Career achievement is an important part of the life I want.
Protecting time outside work is more important to me than maximizing career achievement.
I strongly value maintaining financial independence within a relationship.
I prefer committed partners to combine a substantial part of their finances.
I am comfortable taking substantial financial risks for potentially greater returns.
Religious belief or practice is an important part of my life.
I strongly prefer a partner who shares my fundamental worldview.
I would want my partner to participate with me in religious or spiritual practice.
I am open to serious questions about realities beyond what can be empirically measured.
I can build a close relationship with someone whose fundamental worldview differs from mine.
I would seriously consider relocating for the right long-term relationship.
I have strong reasons to remain in my current region or country.
I could sustain a serious relationship across substantial geographic distance.
I am open to building my life in another country.
Living reasonably close to family is important to me.
Close friendships are a major part of the life I want to maintain.
I want my partner to become integrated into my existing social world.
I prefer a relationship that preserves a strong private world between the partners.
I enjoy having friends or family regularly visit our home.
I expect substantial involvement in caring for or supporting extended family.
Physical attraction is necessary for me to pursue a serious romantic relationship.
I am strongly attracted to a partner's way of thinking and understanding.
Emotional connection is a major source of romantic attraction for me.
Voice, mannerisms, and presence can strongly affect my attraction to someone.
Whether we have children is a relationship-level non-negotiable for me.
The relationship structure must be monogamous for me.
My partner's religious or worldview compatibility is non-negotiable.
There are geographic constraints that a serious relationship cannot realistically overcome.
Certain fundamental lifestyle differences would make a relationship unworkable for me.
A major sexual-compatibility mismatch would make a serious relationship unworkable for me.
In a shared household, I expect responsibilities to be divided explicitly and fairly.
I expect partners to support each other substantially during illness or difficult periods.
I am willing to make significant career compromises for a partner's opportunities.
When finances become difficult, I naturally approach the problem as a shared challenge.
I can remain committed when a partner's interests, priorities, or identity develop substantially over time.
I am willing to take on substantial responsibilities for an aging partner or family member.
A serious relationship should sometimes take priority over individual convenience or plans.
After serious conflict, I actively want to repair the relationship rather than simply move on.
